D.def.1: Spaces, lines, and angles are called given in magnitude to which we can procure equals.
D.def.2: A ratio is said to be given to which we can procure an identical ratio.
D.def.3: Rectilineal figures are said to be given in species whose angles are severally given and the ratios of whose sides to one another are given.
D.def.4: Points, lines, and angles are said to be given in position which always occupy the same place.
D.def.5: A circle is said to be given in magnitude whose radius (straight line from the centre) is given in magnitude.
D.def.6: A circle is said to be given in position and in magnitude whose centre is given in position and whose radius is given in magnitude.
D.def.7: Segments of circles are said to be given in magnitude in which the inscribed angles are given and the bases of the segments are given in magnitude.
D.def.8: Segments of circles are said to be given in position and in magnitude in which the inscribed angles are given in magnitude and the bases of the segments are given in position and in magnitude.
D.def.9: A magnitude is greater than a magnitude by a given magnitude when, the given magnitude being subtracted, the remainder is equal to that same magnitude.
D.def.10: A magnitude is less than a magnitude by a given magnitude when, the given magnitude being added, the whole is equal to that same magnitude.
D.def.11: A magnitude is greater than a magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio when, the given magnitude being subtracted, the remainder has a given ratio to that same magnitude.
D.def.12: A magnitude is less than a magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio when, the given magnitude being added, the whole has a given ratio to that same magnitude.
D.def.13: [A dropped line (katēgmenē) is the straight line drawn from a given point onto a straight line given in position in a given angle.
D.def.14: An erected line (anēgmenē) is the straight line drawn from a given point upon a straight line given in position in a given angle.
D.def.15: Parallel-to-position (para thesei) is the straight line drawn through a given point parallel to a straight line given in position.]
D.1: The ratio of given magnitudes to one another is given.
D.2: If a given magnitude have a given ratio to some other magnitude, that other is also given in magnitude.
D.3: If any multitude of given magnitudes be compounded together, the magnitude compounded out of them will also be given.
D.4: If from a given magnitude a given magnitude be subtracted, the remainder will also be given.
D.5: If a magnitude have a given ratio to a part of itself, it will also have a given ratio to the remainder.
D.6: If two magnitudes having a given ratio to one another be compounded together, the whole magnitude will also have a given ratio to each of them.
D.7: If a given magnitude be divided in a given ratio, each of the segments is given.
D.8: Magnitudes that have given ratios to the same magnitude will also have a given ratio to one another.
D.9: If two or more magnitudes have given ratios to one another, and the same magnitudes have given ratios—even if not the same—to certain other magnitudes, those other magnitudes will also have given ratios to one another.
D.10: If a magnitude be greater than a magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio, the compounded magnitude will also be greater than the same by a given magnitude than in ratio; and if the compounded magnitude be greater than the same by a given magnitude than in ratio, either the remainder is also greater than the same by a given magnitude than in ratio, or the remainder together with the following magnitude to which the other has a given ratio is given.
D.11: If a magnitude be greater than a magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio, the same will also be greater than the compounded magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio; and if the same be greater than the compounded magnitude by a given magnitude than in ratio, the same will also be greater than the remainder by a given magnitude than in ratio.
D.12: If there be three magnitudes, and the first together with the second be given, and the second together with the third be also given, then either the first is equal to the third, or one exceeds the other by a given magnitude.
D.13: If there be three magnitudes, and the first have to the second a given ratio, while the second is greater than the third by a given magnitude than in ratio, the first will also be greater than the third by a given magnitude than in ratio.
D.14: If two magnitudes have a given ratio to one another, and a given magnitude be added to each of them, either the wholes will still have a given ratio to one another, or one will be greater than the other by a given magnitude than in ratio.
D.15: If two magnitudes have a given ratio to one another, and a given magnitude be subtracted from each of them, either the remainders will have a given ratio to one another, or one will be greater than the other by a given magnitude than in ratio.
D.16: If two magnitudes have a given ratio to one another, and from one of them a given magnitude be subtracted while to the other a given magnitude be added, the whole will be greater than the remainder by a given magnitude than in ratio.
D.17: If there be three magnitudes, and the first be greater than the second by a given magnitude than in ratio, and the third be also greater than the same second by a given magnitude than in ratio, then either the first has a given ratio to the third, or one is greater than the other by a given magnitude than in ratio.
D.18: If there be three magnitudes, and one of them be greater than each of the remaining two by a given magnitude than in ratio, the remaining two will either have a given ratio to one another, or one is greater than the other by a given magnitude than in ratio.
D.19: If there be three magnitudes, and the first be greater than the second by a given magnitude than in ratio, and the second be greater than the third by a given magnitude than in ratio, the first will also be greater than the third by a given magnitude than in ratio.
D.20: If there be two given magnitudes, and from them be subtracted magnitudes having a given ratio to one another, either the remainders will have a given ratio to one another, or one is greater than the other by a given magnitude than in ratio.
D.21: If there be two given magnitudes, and there be added to them magnitudes having a given ratio to one another, either the wholes have a given ratio to one another, or one is greater than the other by a given magnitude than in ratio.
D.22: If two magnitudes have a given ratio to some magnitude, the magnitude compounded out of both will also have a given ratio to that same magnitude.
D.23: If a whole have to a whole a given ratio, and the parts have to the parts given ratios, yet not the same ratios, all the parts will have given ratios to all.
D.24: If three straight lines be proportional, and the first have to the third a given ratio, it will also have to the second a given ratio.
D.25: If two lines given in position cut one another, the point at which they cut one another is given in position.
D.26: If the extremities of a straight line be given in position, the straight line is given in position and in magnitude.
D.27: If one extremity of a straight line given in position and in magnitude be given, the other extremity will also be given.
D.28: If through a given point a straight line be drawn parallel to a straight line given in position, the straight line drawn is given in position.
D.29: If to a straight line given in position, and at a given point upon it, a straight line be drawn making a given angle, the straight line drawn is given in position.
D.30: If from a given point a straight line be drawn onto a straight line given in position making a given angle, the straight line drawn is given in position.
D.31: If from a given point onto a straight line given in position a straight line given in magnitude be drawn, it is also given in position.
D.32: If onto parallel straight lines given in position a straight line be drawn making given angles, the straight line cut off between the parallels is given in magnitude.
D.33: If onto parallel straight lines given in position a straight line given in magnitude be drawn, it will make given angles with the parallels.
D.34: If to parallel straight lines given in position a straight line be drawn from a given point, it will be cut in a given ratio.
D.35: If from a given point onto a straight line given in position a straight line be drawn and cut in a given ratio, and through the point of section a parallel be drawn to the straight line given in position, that parallel is given in position.
D.36: If from a given point onto a straight line given in position a straight line be drawn, and there be added to it a straight line having a given ratio to it, and through the extremity a parallel be drawn to the straight line given in position, that parallel is given in position.
D.37: If onto parallel straight lines given in position a straight line be drawn and cut in a given ratio, and through the point of section a parallel be drawn to the parallels given in position, that parallel is given in position.
D.38: If onto parallel straight lines given in position a straight line be drawn, and there be added to it a straight line having a given ratio to it, and through the extremity a parallel be drawn to the parallels given in position, that parallel is given in position.
D.39: If each of the sides of a triangle be given in magnitude, the triangle is given in species.
D.40: If each of the angles of a triangle be given in magnitude, the triangle is given in species.
D.41: If a triangle have one angle given, and the sides about the given angle have a given ratio to one another, the triangle is given in species.
D.42: If the sides of a triangle have given ratios to one another, the triangle is given in species.
D.43: If of a right-angled triangle the sides about one of the acute angles have a given ratio to one another, the triangle is given in species.
D.44: If a triangle have one angle given, and the sides about another angle have a given ratio to one another, the triangle is given in species.
D.45: If a triangle have one angle given, and both the sides together about the given angle have a given ratio to the remaining side, the triangle is given in species.
D.46: If a triangle have one angle given, and the sides together about another angle have a given ratio to the remaining side, the triangle is given in species.
D.47: Rectilineal figures given in species are divided into triangles given in species.
D.48: If on the same straight line two triangles given in species be described, they will have a given ratio to one another.
D.49: If on the same straight line any two rectilineal figures given in species be described, they will have a given ratio to one another.
D.50: If two straight lines have a given ratio to one another, the rectilineal figures similar and similarly described upon them will also have a given ratio to one another.
D.51: If two straight lines have a given ratio to one another, and upon them be described any rectilineal figures given in species, those figures will have a given ratio to one another.
D.52: If on a straight line given in magnitude a rectilineal figure given in species be described, it is given in magnitude.
D.53: If two figures be given in species, and one side of one have a given ratio to one side of the other, the remaining sides will also have given ratios to the remaining sides.
D.54: If two figures given in species have a given ratio to one another, their sides will also have a given ratio to one another.
D.55: If an area be given in species and in magnitude, its sides will also be given in magnitude.
D.56: If two equiangular parallelograms have a given ratio to one another, as a side of the first is to a side of the second, so is the remaining side of the second to that straight line to which the remaining side of the first has the given ratio that the parallelogram has to the parallelogram.
D.57: If a given area be applied to a given straight line in a given angle, the breadth of the application is given.
D.58: If a given area be applied to a given straight line, falling short by a figure given in species, the breadths of the defect are given.
D.59: If a given area be applied to a given straight line, exceeding by a figure given in species, the breadths of the excess are given.
D.60: If a parallelogram given in species and in magnitude be increased or diminished by a gnomon given in magnitude, the breadths of the gnomon are given.
D.61: If along one of the sides of a figure given in species a parallelogrammic area be applied in a given angle, and the figure have a given ratio to the parallelogram, the parallelogram is given in species.
D.62: If two straight lines have a given ratio to one another, and on one of them be described a figure given in species, and on the other a parallelogrammic area in a given angle, and the figure have a given ratio to the parallelogram, the parallelogram is given in species.
D.63: If a triangle be given in species, the square on each of its sides will have a given ratio to the triangle.
D.64: If an obtuse-angled triangle have the obtuse angle given, then that area by which the square on the side subtending the obtuse angle exceeds the squares on the sides containing the obtuse angle will have a given ratio to the triangle.
D.65: If an acute-angled triangle have one acute angle given, then that area by which the square on the side subtending the acute angle is less than the squares on the sides containing the acute angle will have a given ratio to the triangle.
D.66: If a triangle have a given angle, the rectangle contained by the straight lines containing the given angle has a given ratio to the triangle.
D.67: If a triangle have a given angle, then that area by which the square on both the sides containing the given angle taken together as one exceeds the square on the remaining side will have a given ratio to the triangle.
D.68: If two equiangular parallelograms have a given ratio to one another, and one side have to one side a given ratio, the remaining side will also have to the remaining side a given ratio.
D.69: If two parallelograms have given angles, and have a given ratio to one another, and one side have to one side a given ratio, the remaining side will also have a given ratio to the remaining side.
D.70: If of two parallelograms about equal angles, or about unequal yet given angles, the sides have given ratios to one another, the parallelograms themselves will also have a given ratio to one another.
D.71: If of two triangles the sides about equal angles, or about unequal yet given angles, have given ratios to one another, the triangles themselves also have a given ratio to one another.
D.72: If of two triangles both the bases be in a given ratio, and the straight lines drawn onto them from the vertices making either equal angles or unequal yet given angles with the bases be in a given ratio, the triangles themselves will also have a given ratio to one another.
D.73: If of two parallelograms about equal angles, or about unequal yet given angles, the sides stand so that as a side of the first is to a side of the second, so is the remaining side of the second to some other straight line, and the remaining side of the first have a given ratio to that straight line, the parallelograms themselves will also have a given ratio to one another.
D.74: If two parallelograms have a given ratio, either in equal angles or in unequal yet given angles, as a side of the first is to a side of the second, so will the other side of the second be to that straight line to which the remaining side of the first has a given ratio.
D.75: If two triangles have a given ratio to one another, either in equal angles or in unequal yet given angles, as a side of the first is to a side of the second, so will the other side of the second be to that straight line to which the remaining side of the first has a given ratio.
D.76: If in a triangle given in species a perpendicular be drawn from the vertex onto the base, the drawn perpendicular has a given ratio to the base.
D.77: If two figures given in species have a given ratio to one another, any side of one of the figures will also have a given ratio to any side of the other.
D.78: If a given figure have a given ratio to some parallelogram, and one side have a given ratio to one side of the figure, while the parallelogram is in a given angle, the parallelogram will be given in species.
D.79: If there be two triangles having one angle equal to one angle, and from the vertices perpendiculars be drawn to the bases, and as the base of the first triangle is to its perpendicular, so be the base of the second triangle to its perpendicular, the triangles are equiangular.
D.80: If a triangle have one angle given, and the rectangle contained by the sides about the given angle have a given ratio to the square on the remaining side, the triangle is given in species.
D.81: If of three proportional straight lines the extremes have given ratios to the extremes of three proportional straight lines, the means will also have a given ratio to one another; and if an extreme have a given ratio to an extreme and the mean to the mean, the remaining extreme will also have a given ratio to the remaining extreme.
D.82: If four straight lines be proportional, as the first is to that straight line to which the second has a given ratio, so will the third be to that straight line to which the fourth has a given ratio.
D.83: If four straight lines be so related to one another that, when three of them are taken and a fourth is assumed to them to which the remaining one of the original four has a given ratio, the four straight lines are proportional, then as the fourth is to the third, so is the second to that straight line to which the first has a given ratio.
D.84: If two straight lines contain a given area in a given angle, and one exceed the other by a given straight line, each of them will also be given.
D.85: If two straight lines contain a given area in a given angle, and both taken together be given, each of them will also be given.
D.86: If two straight lines contain a given area in a given angle, and the square on one be greater than the square on the other by a given area than in ratio, each of them will also be given.
D.87: If in a circle given in magnitude a straight line be drawn cutting off a segment that accepts a given angle, the straight line drawn is given in magnitude.
D.88: If in a circle given in magnitude a straight line given in magnitude be drawn, it will cut off a segment accepting a given angle.
D.89: If on the circumference of a circle given in position a given point be taken, and from it a straight line be inflected to the circumference of the circle making a given angle, the other extremity of the inflected line is given.
D.90: If from a given point a straight line be drawn touching a circle given in position, the straight line drawn is given in position and in magnitude.
D.91: If a point be taken outside a circle given in position, and from the point some straight line be drawn across the circle, the rectangle contained by the whole drawn straight line and the segment intercepted outside between the point and the convex circumference is given.
D.92: If a point be taken inside a circle given in position, and through the point some straight line be drawn across the circle, the rectangle contained by the segments of the drawn straight line is given.
D.93: If into a circle given in magnitude a straight line be drawn cutting off a segment accepting a given angle, and the angle in the segment be bisected, both the straight lines containing the given angle taken together will have a given ratio to the bisecting chord, and the rectangle contained by both the straight lines containing the given angle taken together and the lower segment cut off from the bisector toward the circumference will be given.
D.94: If in the diameter of a circle given in position a given point be taken, and from that point a straight line be drawn to the circle, and from the section a perpendicular be drawn to the drawn line, and through the point where the perpendicular meets the circumference again a parallel be drawn to the first drawn line, both the point at which the parallel meets the diameter is given, and the rectangle contained by the parallel chords is given.
